title: Electrode Preparation
subtitle: Stable contact before sophisticated interpretation
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating electrode preparation within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain electrode preparation without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in electrode preparation.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to electrode preparation.

sections.explainSimply: Clean skin and secure electrodes help the system measure brain-related voltage rather than unstable contact noise.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Preparation balances signal quality, comfort, infection control and time. Abrasion should be gentle and clinically appropriate.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Document electrode type, conductive medium and preparation method. Monitor skin integrity, allergy and discomfort, especially during repeated sessions.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Trying to tune a faint radio station: contact, interference and antenna placement determine what reaches the speaker.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand electrode preparation to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Aggressive abrasion can injure skin; poor preparation can mimic brain change.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using electrode preparation predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Aggressive abrasion can injure skin; poor preparation can mimic brain change. Evidence classification: established acquisition practice.
